tob-10066: Christian Ginsburg’s nineteenth-century study introduces Kabbalah, the mystical tradition within Judaism, to English readers. He traces how its doctrines of hidden divine mysteries developed over the centuries and surveys the key texts, above all the Zohar. Long out of date in places, the book still serves as a detailed map of a vast and difficult subject.
tob-10466: The second volume of John Calvin’s Institutes completes his system of Reformed doctrine, covering the church, the sacraments, and the Christian life. Here Calvin sets out his famous teaching on predestination alongside practical guidance for prayer, obedience, and civic duty. Together the two volumes became the charter of Presbyterian and Reformed churches worldwide.
tob-0166: Bahá’u’lláh, founder of the Bahá’í faith, wrote the Seven Valleys as a chart of the soul’s road to God — through vales of seeking, love, knowing, oneness, content, wonder, and true poverty. His Persian prose sings with Sufi color. The short work ranks among the best-loved mystic writings of modern times.
tob-12966: James Legge’s Chinese Classics string the heart-books of Confucian teaching — Analects, Great Learning, Mean, Mencius — with the old text and full scholar’s gear. His decades of toil made him the West’s great China-reader. The set stays the groundwork of English Confucian study.
tob-4066: Max Muller’s Rig-Veda is the trail-blazing English of Hinduism’s oldest writ — a thousand and twenty-eight hymns to sky, fire, and storm gods, sung above three thousand years ago. His decades of toil grounded Veda-learning in the West. The volumes stay monuments of Victorian scholarship.
tob-10266: Lévi’s Dogme et Rituel de la Haute Magie — 1854-56 — is the founding text of modern occultism, in its original French. His grand synthesis wed Kabbalah, tarot, and ceremonial magic into one system. Every occultist after him stood on his shoulders. The work remains the bible of the French occult revival.
cia-0000102966: A July 1982 report looking into claims that the Soviets used forced labor to build a giant natural-gas pipeline across Siberia. Pipelines carried Soviet gas to Western Europe, so their construction mattered far beyond Russia's borders. The word alleged matters here: the CIA was weighing reports it could not fully confirm, a common challenge in Cold War intelligence work.
cia-0000109066: A November 1967 report on Cuban-Soviet trade relations, including Moscow's gift of an atomic reactor to Cuba. A Soviet reactor in Havana — even a research one — set off alarms in Washington. The document tracks how economic aid shaded into strategic risk in the Soviet-Cuban partnership.
cia-0000119766: The situation in Hungary as of 9:00 AM on November 1, 1956 — morning of the neutrality declaration. Budapest woke to a free country, or so it seemed. The document captures the dawn of the revolution's climax — hope at its highest, hours before Moscow decided otherwise.
cia-0000126866: A March 1964 report on Babu's agreement to union with Tanganyika — the Zanzibar leader accepting merger into what became Tanzania. The shotgun union followed Zanzibar's bloody revolution by weeks. The document captures nation-building at gunpoint, in real time.
cia-0000126966: A September 1968 Panama situation report — filed a month before the military coup that brought Torrijos to power. The crisis was visible to anyone watching: contested elections, street tension, an army losing patience. The document is the calm before the colonels struck.
cia-0000132266: Situation Report 573 on reactions to an Iraqi move — the truncated title withholds which. By the 570s, the reports chronicled a war in its endgame. The entry is the world's response, catalogued: the diplomacy of defeat.
cia-0000132566: Item 5 in the October 1960 series: the Castro regime planning arms aid to Guatemalan leftists. Havana was exporting guns along with ideology. The document is the arsenal, opening: the revolution, arming its friends.
cia-0000132666: A 1960 report: Cuba preparing for the anniversary of Castro's victory. The revolution was inventing its rituals — parades, speeches, celebrations. The document is the anniversary, planned: the triumph, commemorated.
cia-0000134266: Item 1 in a 1960 general series: Sino-Cuban trade missions arranged. Beijing and Havana were doing business. The document is the mission: the traders, dispatched.
cia-0000135866: A 1952 report on liaison between Calligeris and General Trujillo of Santo Domingo. The Dominican dictator was a fellow traveler in the anti-Arbenz cause. The document is the liaison: the tyrants, cooperating.
cia-0000136166: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN for CHADICK with a message from SEMANTIC for urgent passage — the truncated title cuts off to whom. The urgent relay. The entry is the message: the passage, pressed.
cia-0000136266: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN requesting authorization for bombings to come from LINCOLN itself — the truncated title trails off. The authority to bomb, centralized. The document is the control: the bombings, authorized — from headquarters.
cia-0000136866: A 1954 cable to the senior representative at LINCOLN, personal attention DUNBAR and NOTTING, from WHITING — the archive's spelling says personall. The eyes-only routing. The entry is the attention: the recipients, named.
cia-0000136966: A 1954 cable to the senior representative at LINCOLN on propaganda for the SHERWOOD broadcast. The airwaves content, planned. The document is the material: the propaganda, prepared.
cia-0000138966: An estimated 1987 study of Lebanon's prospects for Islamic fundamentalism — part of the title deleted. The civil war's religious turn, forecast. The document is the prospect: the fundamentalism, weighed.
cia-0000139366: NIE 11-3-61: Sino-Soviet air defense capabilities through mid-1966 — dated 1960 in the archive. The shield, estimated. The document is the defense: the skies, guarded.
cia-0000141166: 1977 excerpts from the transcription of an oral interview conducted by a CIA historian — the truncated title cuts off with whom. The agency's memory, spoken. The document is the interview: the history, oral.
un-ga-res-a-69-66: Resolution A/69/66, adopted in 2014 during the 69th session. The Assembly's business continued. The designation and year are certain; the decision is in the text.
un-sc-res-266: Security Council Resolution 266, adopted in 1969. The Council's business continued. The number and year survive; the decision lives in the text.
un-sc-res-1666: Security Council Resolution 1666, adopted in 2006 — aligned. The Council's business rolled on. The number and year endure; the decision is in the text.
un-sc-res-1866: Security Council Resolution 1866, adopted in 2009 — aligned. The Council's business continued. The number and year survive; the decision lives in the text.
un-sc-res-1966: Security Council Resolution 1966, adopted in December 2010 — the Residual Mechanism resolution, creating the body to finish the work of the Yugoslavia and Rwanda tribunals. The courts' legacy, preserved. The resolution is the mechanism: the justice, residual.
cia-0000132766: A 1960 CIA Cuba file — number 0000132766. Another folder in the 1960 Cuba run. The entry is the run: the year, covered.
cia-0000136566: A 1960 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents, numbered 0000136566. The training year's record closed here. The document is the record: the training, documented.
cia-0000136766: An estimated 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents — number 0000136766, the archive's date uncertain. The circa set. The document is the circa: the dating, soft.
cia-0000139466: A 1988 CIA Project Sun Streak file — number 0000139466. The mind-spies, one more dossier. The entry is the dossier: the viewing, remote.
un-sc-res-166: Security Council Resolution 166, adopted in 1961 — aligned. The early-sixties Council deciding. The designation and year endure; the act is in the text.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d66: The Acting Secretary of State Stettinius to the President, October 28 — the truncated title cuts off the year — Document 66. The stand-in secretary wrote. The memo is the stand-in's: Stettinius, briefing.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d166: A memorandum by the British members of the Moscow Conference committee on — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 166. The British committee members' paper. The memo is the committee's: the members, British.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d266: An editorial note — Cairo-Tehran 1943, Document 266. The editors' seam. The note is the seam: the narrative, stitched.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d366: Bohlen minutes, November 29, 1943 — Document 366. A second that day. The minutes are the doubling: the day, busy.
arxiv-2605-08966: Transformers remember through attention, but distant words fade. Nabil Mlaiki proposes VORT, giving transformers an adaptive power-law memory — a forgetting curve borrowed from psychology, tuned on the fly. The 2026 paper rethinks how language models hold onto the distant past.
arxiv-2605-09166: How many rational points can a smooth surface in three-dimensional projective space hold over a finite field? Yves Aubry and José Felipe Voloch attack the question head-on. The 2026 paper is arithmetic geometry, counting solutions where number theory meets geometry.
arxiv-2605-09266: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards now spans modalities — but does training blind in one modality transfer to another? Kun Xiang, Terry Jingchen Zhang, Zirong Liu, and colleagues diagnose modality transfer and blind-training effects with SeePhysPro. The 2026 paper is multimodal RL diagnostics.
arxiv-2605-09366: Analyzing brain scans takes expert neuroscientists, and there are never enough of them. Keqi Han, Songlin Zhao, Yao Su, and colleagues move toward a virtual neuroscientist via multi-agent collaboration on neuroimaging analysis. The 2026 paper is AI teamwork for brain science.
arxiv-2605-09466: Achlioptas processes build random graphs with a choice at each step — and bounded-size rules keep that choice local and analyzable. Mihyun Kang and Oliver Riordan count subgraphs as these processes evolve. The 2026 paper is probabilistic combinatorics on controlled randomness.
arxiv-2605-09766: Centralizers — the full set of everything commuting with a given group — reveal the group's inner structure. Tadej Starčič computes them explicitly for the complex orthogonal and symplectic groups. The 2026 paper is classical Lie theory with explicit, genuinely usable answers.
plos-pone-0003466: Physiologists found men's and women's muscles hear hunger signals differently in this 2008 study. Leptin, the satiety hormone, docks at receptors on skeletal muscle, and the team compared receptor levels, blood leptin, and insulin sensitivity between the sexes. The gender gap in this signaling may help explain differences in metabolism and diabetes risk.
plos-pone-0003566: Psychologists found music lessons tuning young minds in this 2008 study. Children who practiced a musical instrument showed stronger verbal ability and nonverbal reasoning than their peers. The association held beyond music-specific skills, suggesting that sustained instrumental training may sharpen broader cognitive powers.
plos-pone-0003666: In 2008, a team showed faces swaying votes by gender. Voters judged the faces of those running, and those snap reads predicted voting, but the reads tilted by the runner's gender. The work exposes a facial bias: how a leader looks moves ballots differently for men and women.
plos-pone-0003766: Vogt, D'Angelo, and Oswald pulled a light switch from the deep sea in this 2008 paper. Their new green fluorescent protein, found in a deep-sea creature, can be switched on and off with light. The photoswitchable marker gives cell biologists a sharper tool for live imaging.
plos-pone-0003866: In 2008, a team compared fast-aging fish strains. The short-lived annual killifish Nothobranchius furzeri showed large aging differences between strains. The strain comparison turns this tiny fish into a powerful model for studying why we age.
plos-pone-0003966: In 2008, Tan, Schedl, and Song linked an immune pathway to Alzheimer's damage in flies. Toll-to-NF-kB signaling mediated the harmful effects of the human amyloid-beta 42 peptide. The fly model implicates innate immunity in neurodegeneration.
plos-pone-0004066: In 2008, Mine, Fortunel, and Pageon found skin aging is layer-deep. Aging altered the function of papillary dermal fibroblasts. Reticular fibroblasts, sitting deeper, stayed unchanged. The split view recasts how the dermis drives wrinkles. Targeting the upper layer could guide future anti-wrinkle care.
plos-pone-0004166: In 2009, Courtney, Ofek, and Penfound linked germ slipperiness to stickiness. M protein and lipoteichoic acid levels set how germs shun water. The surface traits fed sticking and biofilm growth in strep germs. The neat link exposes targets for future anti-stick drugs.
plos-pone-0004366: In 2009, Gingerich, ul-Haq, and von Koenigswald found a whale born on land. A new protocetid whale from Pakistan's middle Eocene showed land birth and precocial young. The four-legged predator predated true whales by millions of years. The fossil bridges land and sea beautifully.
plos-pone-0358966: Lectures, bedside teaching, group work — medical students at Nigeria’s Abubakar Tafawa Balewa University were asked which teaching methods they actually prefer. This survey paper reports their answers and what shapes them, from class size to exam style. The findings give the school practical guidance for training future doctors in the ways they learn best.
plos-pone-0358066: People living with HIV face higher cancer risks, but the pattern in Uganda was poorly mapped. This retrospective study at a specialized HIV center catalogued the spectrum of tumors and their immune and viral drivers. The results give Ugandan oncologists a clearer picture of which cancers to screen for in HIV care.
plos-pone-0358566: Gun violence in the West Bank leaves a trail of injuries that few studies have documented. This multicenter paper traces the epidemiology, injury patterns, treatment, and outcomes of firearm injuries across the region. The data give health planners and trauma teams the first solid picture of who gets shot, how badly, and what saves them.
plos-pone-0358366: Not knowing what your cancer will do next is its own torment. This paper used latent profile analysis to map illness uncertainty in women with gynecologic and breast cancer. The distinct uncertainty profiles point to which patients need the most support navigating the unknown.
plos-pone-0357466: What do kids actually think of natural history museums? This paper captured children’s perceptions through Portugal’s ‘Young Naturalists’ program. Their insights tell museum educators what fascinates young visitors — dinosaurs, hands-on exhibits, live animals — and what leaves them cold, guiding better programs.
plos-pone-0356366: Locking up petty offenders might manufacture more criminals, not fewer. This paper modeled the dark side of prison dynamics, quantifying the criminogenic effects of incarcerating petty crime offenders. The numbers put a measurable price on the school-of-crime effect that reformers have long warned about.
plos-pone-0346466: Spotty liver disease costs the egg industry millions in lost production. This paper mapped the hepatic transcriptomic landscape of chickens to reveal host responses to the disease. The gene-level picture shows how birds fight back at the molecular level — and where future vaccines might lend a hand.
plos-pone-0358266: Babies born with duct-dependent lung circulation need a lifeline: a ductal stent or a Blalock–Taussig shunt. This paper compared outcomes of pulmonary artery changes between the two approaches. The head-to-head results guide heart surgeons choosing the safer bridge to definitive repair in these fragile newborns.
plos-pone-0358466: Cancer treatment can steal fertility — but many survivors still become mothers against the odds. This Taiwanese population-based study measured rates of childbirth in female cancer survivors. The rates give survivors realistic hope and give doctors solid data for honest fertility counseling.
plos-pone-0357966: Chronic low oxygen rewires the heart and scrambles its internal clock. This paper showed sustained hypoxia induces divergent response patterns in cardiac metabolic-immune adaptation and circadian rhythm regulation. The split responses reveal how hearts cope with thin air — adapting in some systems while faltering in others.
plos-pone-0356266: Passion fruit viruses threaten harvests across the tropics — and early detection is everything. This paper established and validated a real-time fluorescence quantitative PCR assay for detecting EAPV in Passiflora edulis. The test hands growers a fast, reliable way to catch infection before it spreads.
plos-pone-0357666: Esports for seniors sounds like a joke — but the results are serious. This non-randomized pilot trial tested the feasibility and effects of a multicomponent program incorporating esports on physical and cognitive function among older adults. The feasibility results open a surprising door to keeping aging minds and bodies active.
plos-pone-0356566: Measuring leg strength accurately on the leg press demands the right loading strategy. This paper identified the optimal two-point loading strategy for accurate leg press force–velocity assessment. The validated protocol gives sports scientists trustworthy strength profiles.
plos-pone-0355466: Natural product drug screening is plagued by false alarms from pan-assay interference compounds. This paper proposed a bioactivity-leveling approach for component-specific evaluation, optimizing SARS-CoV-2 antiviral screening by controlling for those nuisance compounds. The method separates genuine antiviral hits from chemical noise.
plos-pone-0356766: South Korea’s AI ethical principles needed a refresh after five fast-moving years. This paper supplemented the original principles with a five-year update. The revised framework grapples with generative AI and other developments the first version never imagined.
plos-pone-0354366: Dentists see smokers regularly — a missed opportunity for cessation counseling. This cross-sectional study captured views from patients and dentists as key stakeholders on smoking cessation counseling in primary dental care. The dual perspectives reveal why the dental chair remains an underused front in the fight against tobacco.
plos-pone-0355866: Cities drown in stormwater — but compost-amended soil can drink it up. This paper showed compost incorporation improves infiltration rates and associated soil hydro-physical properties as a stormwater management intervention. The humble amendment turns compacted urban ground into a sponge — a cheap, green defense against flooding.
plos-pone-0354966: Choosing how many components a model needs — and how much to shrink them — is usually guesswork. This paper developed automatic uncertainty evaluation for determining component numbers in nested models and shrinkage regularization parameters. The automated approach replaces arbitrary choices with principled, uncertainty-aware selection.
plos-pone-0347366: Gene regulation evolves — but do regulatory connections survive across species? This ortholog transfer stress test examined regulatory edge conservation across species, tissues, and evolutionary distance. The findings reveal which regulatory wiring evolution preserves — fundamental knowledge for comparative genomics.
plos-pone-0355166: Measuring tobacco smoke exposure in Saudi women — where smoking is stigmatized — needs objective biomarkers. This paper assessed exposure via urinary cotinine analysis. The biomarker data reveal true exposure levels that self-reports miss — essential for honest tobacco control policy.
plos-pone-0356066: Screening for adverse childhood experiences — in clinic versus by phone — yields different answers. This paper compared ACEs reporting between clinic and telephone-based screening. The mode comparison reveals how setting shapes disclosure of childhood trauma — critical for screening program design.
plos-pone-0354466: Detecting objects through bad weather — rain, fog, darkness — needs RGB fused with thermal vision. This paper proposed a two-stage graph-based framework for all-weather RGB-T object detection that recovers weak signals. The framework promises reliable machine vision when conditions defeat ordinary cameras.
europmc-pmc2814866: Fat tissue is not just storage, it is active biology, and this 2010 paper profiles its microRNA regulators. The authors map miRNA expression in human subcutaneous fat and track how it changes as fat cells mature. The profile reveals which tiny RNAs steer fat development. The data became a resource for obesity and metabolism research.
europmc-pmc2815666: A companion to the XDS paper, this 2010 article by Wolfgang Kabsch covers the next steps in crystallography data processing. It explains integration, scaling, space-group assignment, and post-refinement, the stages that convert raw measurements into accurate data. The paper is a practical guide to getting the numbers right. Together with XDS, it standardized a field.
europmc-pmc2831066: The amyloid beta protein blamed in Alzheimer's may have a day job fighting germs. This 2010 paper reports that it acts as an antimicrobial peptide, killing microbes in lab tests. The authors propose its brain buildup might start as immune defense gone wrong. The provocative finding reframed a notorious molecule as part of innate immunity.
europmc-pmc2851566: One DNA patch, 9p21, kept turning up in diseases from heart trouble to tumors. This 2010 paper ties its SNPs to many disease forms and links them to ANRIL, a nearby RNA. The team bared a shared root. The find hinted one patch may steer several diseases.
europmc-pmc2897766: Cells tune their stress response with exquisite care. This 2010 paper shows BiP binding to the stress sensor Ire1 tunes the unfolded protein response's homeostatic behavior. The authors' quantitative work reveals the dial. Their finding matters for diseases of protein misfolding.
europmc-pmc2911766: Surgery patients do better when fluids are tuned, not poured. This 2010 randomized study tests fluid tuning with stroke volume variation in high-risk surgery patients. The authors show guided fluids beat fixed doses. Their result changed how anesthesia teams handle fluids.
europmc-pmc3013466: Disgust evolved to keep us from disease. This 2011 paper argues the yuck response is a disease-avoidance system. The authors make the evolutionary case. Their work reframed a basic emotion. Rotten smells trigger the ancient alarm. Moral disgust may borrow the same wiring.
europmc-pmc6522366: Two mosquitoes - Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus - carry dengue, Zika, yellow fever, and chikungunya, and their territory keeps growing. This study maps where the vectors have spread and models where climate and travel will take them next. Knowing the future front lines helps health agencies aim mosquito control before outbreaks arrive.
europmc-pmc6548966: Growing a replacement heart patch - thick, with its own blood vessels, matched to the patient - has been a pipe dream. Israeli researchers 3D-printed just that: cardiac patches and even mini-hearts with working vessel networks, built from a patient's own cells. The printed tissues beat in the dish, bringing personalized heart repair a step closer.
europmc-pmc6558766: One in six American mothers in a landmark survey reported mistreatment during pregnancy or childbirth - being shouted at, ignored, or pressured into procedures. The Giving Voice to Mothers study, designed with patients and advocates, documents inequity in maternity care, hitting women of color hardest. The findings demand safer, more respectful birth care for all.
europmc-pmc6567666: A genome-scale metabolic model is a digital twin of a cell's chemistry - every gene linked to the reactions it drives. This review surveys the state of these models: how they are built, how they predict what cells will do, and where they are used, from biofuels to medicine. The models turn genomes into testable predictions.
europmc-pmc6626766: Designer nanoparticles promise to outsmart cancer's defenses: homing to tumors, slipping past barriers, and releasing drugs on cue. This review surveys the trends and challenges of engineered nanomaterials in cancer therapy - targeting, safety, and the long road to the clinic. The tiny tools carry big hopes and real hurdles.
europmc-pmc6627766: Eating all your meals early - time-restricted feeding - may steady blood sugar around the clock. In a controlled trial, early eaters saw better 24-hour glucose and shifts in circadian markers. The study suggests when you eat matters as much as what, with the body clock as the mediator.
europmc-pmc6647366: Solid tumors outgrow their blood supply, turning acidic and oxygen-starved - conditions where carbonic anhydrase IX thrives. This review traces CA IX's role in helping cancers survive hypoxia and acidosis. Because healthy tissues barely use it, the enzyme is an attractive bullseye for therapy.
europmc-pmc6670166: New to systematic reviews? This step-by-step guide walks beginners through one using simulated data - from question to search to analysis. Built for tropical medicine but useful anywhere, it demystifies the methods behind evidence synthesis. A friendly on-ramp to a daunting task.
europmc-pmc6683166: Could a gut transplant fight Alzheimer's? In mice engineered to develop the disease, fecal microbiota transplants eased brain pathology - fewer plaques, calmer inflammation. The mouse study hints the gut-brain axis runs both ways, opening a wild new therapeutic frontier.
europmc-pmc6718566: PD-L1 is cancer's invisibility cloak - it tells T cells to stand down. This review surveys the protein's distribution and the three ways to defeat it: blocking antibodies, genetic knockdown, or small-molecule inhibition. Each strategy has trade-offs, and the comparison guides the next wave of checkpoint therapy.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-266: From the Government Accountability Office's 2007 series, this report analyzes how the IRS uses third-party information returns — the W-2s, 1099s, and similar forms filed by employers and banks. It tallies what it costs to collect and match those forms against tax returns, and measures how much revenue that matching recovers. The findings weigh the efficiency of one of the tax system's most powerful compliance tools.
gao-gaoreports-b-310066: A 2007 ruling from GAO, the office that settles fights over federal contracts. Eggs & Bacon, Inc. said an agency picked the wrong winner, and this ruling lays out both sides plus the final call. Like all GAO protest rulings, it follows the rules Congress set for fair bidding — and it stands as a guide for future contract fights.
gao-gaoreports-gao-08-166: This 2007 GAO report audits the tax collector itself — the IRS's own books for 2007 and 2006. An outside audit team dug into its accounts, cash controls, and money reports. The report hands down a formal grade plus any big flaws found: a yearly physical for the agency that touches every paycheck in America.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-866: The Navy's floating giant was busting its budget in 2007 — GAO's report says building the carrier Gerald R. Ford on budget looked grim. New tech and rosy estimates collided on the biggest ship ever attempted. The findings are a case study in how defense megaprojects drift from the dock of affordability.
gao-gaoreports-b-299766: Lockheed Martin's maritime arm took its August 2007 contract fight to GAO — two case numbers, one sea-systems prize. The combined ruling sorts the defense giant's claims against procurement law. Naval tech deals draw the fiercest bid wars, and GAO's call is the harbor master.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-466: Doctor pay had a geography problem in 2007 — GAO's report says Medicare's cost-of-practice map needed redrawing. The findings show the payment zones no longer matched reality. The report argues that where a doctor heals should not warp what healing pays.
gao-gaoreports-b-299266: Solec Corporation took its March 2007 contract fight to GAO, and this ruling is the verdict on the claims. The firm said the agency's award was unfair, and the call tests the protest. Solar names get the same full hearing as everyone.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-166: Closing bases left toxic cleanup bills in 2007, and GAO's report says the cost reporting could improve and the land transfers should speed up. The findings press for action. The report warns that the shuttered forts should not stay fenced forever. The dirt had to be cleaned and conveyed.
openalex-w7204793266: Alzheimer's steals memory and changes behavior, and drugs can only do so much. This paper reviews music therapy as an added way to ease symptoms: how melodies and rhythm affect mood, agitation, and well-being in patients. The authors gather what research says about music as medicine for dementia. Gentle and hopeful, it explores a treatment with no side effects and deep human roots.
openalex-w7163065466: New glowing molecules start with clever lab work. This paper reports cooking up boranils, light-emitting boron compounds, with an iodine-driven reaction, then testing what they do. The authors tuned the recipe to waste little. A molecule-making study of tiny lights bound for scans and screens.
openalex-w7128963966: Magnets on a lattice can freeze into competing orders, and this paper maps the border. The authors used numerical diagonalization, exact computer solution of small systems, to find where the dimer phase gives way to magnetic order in a spin-2 antiferromagnet. They compared the results with earlier work. A computational study of quantum magnetism's phase lines.
openalex-w4410722266: Superconductors push magnets away, but atomic hearts still feel the pull. This lab paper measured a nuclear signal, the Knight shift, at two atom spots in the superconductor LaRu4P12 under magnetic fields. The team read out how spins respond. A precision study of magnetism hiding inside a superconductor.
pmc-13475966: A 2026 virology paper about Oropouche virus testing. Labs normally need blood serum from past patients as a positive control, but the team engineered a human-mouse chimeric antibody — a lab-made protein — that can stand in for it. Having a reliable, on-demand control makes diagnostic tests for this emerging virus easier and safer to run worldwide.
pmc-13480266: A 2026 medical education piece on diagnostic anchoring — the trap of locking onto an early diagnosis and ignoring evidence against it. Written for clinicians, it walks through how the bias takes hold and how doctors can catch themselves. Short and practical, it is aimed at making everyday diagnosis safer.
pmc-13478866: In this 2026 paper, the authors built ActivityDiff, a diffusion model — the same AI family behind image generators — steered by positive and negative activity signals to design new drug molecules from scratch. Guiding generation toward active and away from inactive chemistry could make de novo design far more efficient. The paper demonstrates the approach on drug targets.
pmc-13466866: In this 2026 hematology study, researchers compared helper T-cell subset activity and cytokine signatures in sickle cell patients who develop alloimmunisation — immune reactions against transfused blood. Understanding which immune profiles predict the reaction could make transfusions safer. The cytokine signatures are a step toward that prediction.
pmc-13385466: A 2026 neuropathology review on the diagnostic challenges of choroid plexus tumors — rare brain tumors arising in the fluid-producing tissue. Their rarity makes diagnosis treacherous. The paper walks through the pitfalls and how to avoid them.
pmc-13402866: A 2026 study finding that the length of embryo culture in assisted reproductive technology does not have a major impact on newborn DNA methylation. Epigenetic worries about longer culture appear largely unfounded. The reassuring result matters to fertility clinics and parents.
pmc-13598566: This 2026 Chinese-language paper examines models for building youth mental health service systems under different institutional backgrounds, and draws lessons for China. Comparing international systems offers policy options. The paper is a comparative policy study written for a Chinese audience.
pmc-13429466: A 2026 review asking what hibernators and other adapted animals can teach us about organ transplantation — their mechanisms of cold resistance and enhanced regeneration. Nature solved organ preservation long ago. The paper mines animal biology for transplant advances.
pmc-13624266: A 2026 immunology paper showing platelet-derived serotonin epigenetically programs macrophage alternative activation to orchestrate type 2 airway inflammation. Platelets moonlight as immune programmers. The epigenetic mechanism is the discovery.
pmc-13634766: A 2026 NLP data paper on a multilingual annotated dataset for metadata extraction from Persian, Arabic, and English scientific articles. The annotations train extraction models. The multilinguality is the value.
pmc-13530666: This 2026 conference poster ("PASS or Fail") identified predictors of poor outcome after arthroscopic posterior labral repair in a multi-surgeon prospective cohort. The predictors guide expectations. The poster names them.
pmc-13448266: This 2026 conference abstract (RMTC-03) evaluated "brain permeability" — a critical issue for developing drugs to reduce brain metastasis incidence. Getting drugs past the blood-brain barrier is the challenge. The abstract frames the issue.
pmc-13544966: This 2026 review covered stem cell-based therapeutics in epilepsy — current advances and future prospects. The regenerative approach to seizures is emerging. The review surveys the field.
pmc-13492266: A 2026 correction notice for a paper titled "PFAS Toxicity: What's True, What's Not, and What Really Matters." Corrections amend the record. This entry preserves the correction.
pmc-13469066: A 2026 paper showing CHK2 regulates MUS81-dependent double-strand breaks in response to replication stress and BRCA2 deficiency. The checkpoint kinase controlled the breaks. The regulation matters for cancer therapy.
pmc-13525366: In this 2026 Mexican study, exposure to Coccidioides species and silent infection in Sonora were analyzed via cross-sectional serological and environmental analysis. The valley fever fungus's silent spread was mapped. The analysis informs public health.
pmc-13462366: In this 2026 conservation paper, escalating fire-driven forest loss in protected tropical forests was documented. The protected areas burned anyway. The escalation is the alarm.
